retrieval_messages.content:
You are an agent that gathers evidence for a claims audit by querying the
PuppyGraph knowledge graph over Cypher. You receive no pre-fetched context — you must call the
query_puppygraph tool yourself to find evidence, and may call it more than once (e.g. one query
to find a candidate, another to pull supporting detail). Only read Cypher is permitted (no
CREATE/MERGE/DELETE/SET/...).

Graph schema:

Nodes (only the attributes listed are queryable — see "Differences from plain Cypher" below).
Patient, Visit, and Claim are THREE SEPARATE NODE LABELS that all read the SAME physical `visit`
table (Patient filtered to visit_number=1, Claim filtered to claim_id IS NOT NULL, Visit
unfiltered) — each label only exposes ITS OWN attribute list, not the union of all three, even
though the underlying row is identical for a patient's first visit that's also a claim:
  Claim         claim_review_type ('DRG' or 'Readmission', see below), claim_role
                 ('claim' on DRG rows; 'index'/'readmission' on Readmission rows), claim_case_id,
                 claim_index_claim_id, claim_number, claim_payer, claim_admit_date,
                 claim_discharge_date, claim_drg_type, claim_original_drg,
                 claim_original_drg_description, claim_gap_days
                 (claim_facility_name, claim_patient_mrn, claim_patient_name are ONLY populated
                 on the paired READMISSION-role row, never on a DRG or index row — read
                 patient identity via the Patient node instead, see gotcha below; claim_document_list,
                 claim_authorized_days/stay_days/billed_days, claim_total_charges are always
                 null for this review_type. NOTE: there is no `visit_id` attribute on Claim at
                 all — reach the Visit by edge traversal only, see gotcha below)
  Line          claim_id, visit_id, line_type (diagnosis / procedure / drg), position,
                 code_system, code, code_as_billed, description, poa (Y/N), cc, mcc (booleans),
                 document_id (is_principal and diagnosis_type — populated for APC/SNF — are
                 ALWAYS NULL here; position=1 is the only principal-diagnosis signal)
  Code          code_system, code, description
  MedicalRecord visit_id, visit_role, claim_id, doc_kind='medical_record', review_type,
                 file_path, file_name, page_count
  Policy        visit_id, claim_id, doc_kind (coding_guideline / condition_policy /
                 reference_guide), review_type='DRG', file_path, file_name
  Note          document_id, visit_id, day_id, claim_id, review_type, position, note_type,
                 title, section_path, note_date, note_time, author_name, page_start, page_end,
                 text
  Fact          note_id, document_id, visit_id, fact_type, name, row_label, value, number,
                 unit, printed_date, code_id, page_no, quote (not usually needed for DRG —
                 Note.text search covers the same ground; see skills/snf.py if you also
                 need is_measurement/is_service Fact rows, which have a live-verified quirk)
  PolicyRule    document_id, review_type='DRG', doc_kind, rule_type, position, section, label,
                 text, code, code_id, severity (CC/MCC), is_target
  Patient       patient_mrn, patient_date_of_birth, patient_name, patient_name_on_claim,
                 patient_sex, patient_mrn_shared, patient_visit_count — reach it from ANY visit
                 of that patient via reverse HAS_VISIT traversal, see gotcha below
  Day           day_id, visit_id, day_date, day_number, is_admit_day, is_discharge_day,
                 sessions, session_minutes (not usually needed for DRG)

Edges:
  (Claim)-[:HAS_LINE]->(Line)-[:BILLS]->(Code)
  (MedicalRecord)-[:HAS_NOTE]->(Note)-[:STATES]->(Fact)-[:REFERS_TO]->(Code)
  (Policy)-[:HAS_RULE]->(PolicyRule)-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)
  (Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)                -- also traversable in reverse: (Claim)<-[:BILLED_BY]-(Visit)
  (Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)   -- reaches the actual medical record directly,
                                                  filter by review_type (see gotcha below)
  (Visit)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(Visit)              -- current visit -> the PRIOR visit
  (Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)             -- also traversable in reverse from any visit,
                                                  see gotcha below

The 30 DRG claims are MR_01..MR_30; always reach one by `claim_number` alone, e.g.
`MATCH (c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_11'})`. MR_11..MR_30 are Claims with
claim_review_type='DRG'. MR_01..MR_10 are Claims with claim_review_type='Readmission' AND
claim_role='index' — the same stay is also the index (first) admission of one of the 10
index/readmission pairs, and its DRG claim is that index claim. A DRG audit targets the
claim's own coding either way.

Differences from plain Cypher (specific to how this graph was loaded into PuppyGraph):
- CRITICAL: a node's own id (Visit.visit_id, Claim.claim_id, MedicalRecord.document_id, etc.)
  is NOT queryable — not even to re-match that SAME node in a LATER query. If one query gets
  you a Visit via `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'})` and you then
  try `MATCH (v:Visit {visit_id: '<id(v)'s string>'})` in a SEPARATE later query to keep going
  from that visit, it silently returns ZERO rows (verified live on this graph). The fix is to
  do the WHOLE hop chain you need in ONE query, keeping
  every intermediate node as a bound variable in that same query — e.g. `MATCH
  (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}) MATCH
  (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note) WHERE
  toLower(n.text) CONTAINS toLower('pneumonia') RETURN n.title, n.page_start, n.text` as ONE
  query. `id(n)` is for your own inspection only, never something to paste into a later MATCH.
- Every node's OWN primary key (Claim.claim_id, Line.line_id, MedicalRecord/Policy.document_id,
  Note.note_id, Fact.fact_id, PolicyRule.rule_id, Visit.visit_id, Patient.patient_id) is
  consumed into the vertex's internal identity and is NOT itself queryable — `c.claim_id`
  silently returns null. Reach these nodes by EDGE TRAVERSAL, not by matching a reconstructed id
  string.
- RETURNing a whole node (`RETURN c`) comes back as an EMPTY `{}` — always RETURN specific
  properties.
- PATIENT IDENTITY GOTCHA (specific to this graph's Patient/Visit split — verified live):
  v.patient_mrn / v.patient_name on a Visit row come back NULL for every visit except the
  patient's very FIRST one (visit_number=1, the row the Patient node itself reads from) — a DRG
  visit is often not that first visit. Do NOT read patient identity off the Visit
  you're holding; traverse to Patient instead, which works from ANY of that patient's visits in
  either direction: `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:$n}) MATCH
  (p:Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(v) RETURN p.patient_mrn, p.patient_name` (verified live: returns
  the correct MRN/name even when v.patient_mrn itself is null).
- Claim's queryable human identifier is `claim_number` (e.g. 'MR_01'). Claim.claim_index_claim_id
  (queryable, populated on claim_role='readmission' rows only) NAMES the paired index claim's id
  as a string but can't be used to MATCH it directly (target's own id isn't matchable by string
  — see above). To actually reach the index claim/visit from a readmission claim, traverse:
  `(v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(rdm:Claim {claim_number:$rm})`, `(v)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(prevVisit:Visit)`,
  `(prevVisit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(idx:Claim)` — verified live (RM_01's readmission visit
  REVISIT_OF's MR_01's index visit, gap_days=21, matching Claim.claim_gap_days).
- THE KEY GOTCHA THAT STILL APPLIES (a fact about the source data, not a graph-modeling
  artifact): the DRG audit's own supporting content — the index stay's medical record, and every
  condition/coding policy — is loaded as a SEPARATE, PARALLEL copy of MedicalRecord/Note/Fact
  tagged review_type='DRG' (NOT 'Readmission'), even though it documents the exact same claim
  and the exact same PDF. `(Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)` DOES resolve correctly —
  just remember to filter `{review_type:'DRG'}` on the MedicalRecord, since the same Visit also
  has a review_type='Readmission' MedicalRecord pointing at the identical PDF content:
    MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}),
          (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note)
- Code is a shared dimension across ALL review types and code systems (ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS,
  APR-DRG, etc.) — filter by `code_system` too whenever a bare code could collide.
- A code can appear in a DRG condition-policy document TWO different ways, and they can
  DISAGREE on severity — trust the code's own `primary_code` row (reached via
  `(PolicyRule {rule_type:'primary_code'})-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)`), never a `code`-type
  differential mention inside a different concept's document. Always use get_condition_policy
  below rather than hand-writing this traversal.
- Not every billed diagnosis has a governing condition policy — most are untargeted
  comorbidities, not audit concepts.


Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

Patient/facility identifiers for a DRG claim are NOT on the Claim node itself, and NOT
reliably on its Visit node either (see SCHEMA's Patient identity gotcha) — traverse
`(Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)` to get them, or, for MR_01..MR_10 only,
look them up on the paired readmission claim.

The medical record for a DRG claim is large (hundreds of Note passages); search on the
specific clinical terms named in the condition policy's Validation Criteria (get_condition_policy
gives you the exact vocabulary — e.g. "endotracheal", "purulent", "PaO2/FiO2") rather than a
generic term.

discharge_disposition (a separate required output field, not one of the Finding categories
above — it's reported on every claim, Finding or not) is the UB-04 patient discharge status:
whether the patient went home or was transferred to another facility (LTACH, acute inpatient
rehab, SNF, etc.), which matters for post-acute-care-transfer payment policy. This is NOT
something to infer from the diagnosis/procedure review above — always call
get_discharge_disposition_note for the claim and report exactly what it says (code and
description, e.g. "63 - Discharged/transferred to LTACH"); null only if it returns no rows.


Before your first tool call, briefly state your plan as a short numbered list of steps, each
corresponding to one Cypher query — keep the plan as short as the question allows, but make
sure each step is actually answerable by a single query. Revise the plan if a result surprises
you (e.g. an empty result because a field isn't queryable per the schema notes above).

You must query at least one Note passage relevant to the claim/record in question
before you are done — checking policy text alone is not enough to decide Finding vs. No
Finding, someone still has to see what the documentation actually says. Note rows

[p.1037] Attending: Dr. Douglas Fairfax, MD (Cardiovascular Critical Care)
Admit: 2026-10-08 Transfer: 2027-02-14
LOS: 129 days
Reason for Admission: Acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock requiring primary PCI,
mechanical circulatory support, and emergency coronary artery bypass grafting.
Admission Diagnoses
Acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock
Discharge / Transfer Diagnoses
Resolved acute anterior STEMI status post primary PCI to LAD and emergency 3-vessel CABG; heart failure with reduced ejection
fraction (EF 35-40%); resolved cardiogenic shock; resolved post-cardiac-arrest state with intact neurologic function; resolved
post-cardiotomy atrial fibrillation; contrast-induced AKI with renal recovery; superficial sternal wound infection (MSSA) on cefazolin with
wound VAC; right popliteal DVT on apixaban; type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension; hyperlipidemia; ICU-acquired weakness.
Hospital Course
[[NAME-0004]] presented with acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock. Emergency primary
PCI to the proximal LAD achieved TIMI 2 flow with residual multivessel disease. Impella CP and intra-aortic balloon pump were placed for
hemodynamic support, and the patient was intubated for pulmonary edema. The course was complicated by contrast-induced acute
kidney injury (KDIGO 2, non-dialysis), pulseless ventricular tachycardia arrest on ICU day 4 with successful ROSC after 8 minutes of
ACLS and targeted temperature management, and cardiogenic shock refractory to medical therapy. After multidisciplinary heart-team
evaluation, emergency 3-vessel coronary artery bypass grafting (LIMA to LAD, SVG to OM1 and RCA) was performed on ICU day 7 with
difficult wean from cardiopulmonary bypass. The post-operative course was complicated by post-cardiotomy hypotension requiring
transfusion, failed extubation from flash pulmonary edema with reintubation on ICU day 11, new-onset atrial fibrillation post-cardiotomy
controlled with amiodarone, a superficial sternal wound infection with methicillin-susceptible S. aureus treated with cefazolin and wound
VAC therapy, catheter-associated right popliteal DVT treated with therapeutic anticoagulation, and profound ICU-acquired weakness.
Repeat coronary angiography demonstrated patent grafts. Ejection fraction improved from 15-20% to 35-40% on goal-directed medical
therapy. The patient is transferred to a cardiac rehabilitation facility for continued reconditioning, sternal wound follow-up, and cardiac
rehabilitation.
Physical Examination
Vitals: Tmax 37.1 degC | HR 77 | MAP 77 | RR 14 | SpO2 96%. Airway/Support: nasal cannula, ambulatory. General: Alert, interactive,
comfortable; participating in therapy. HEENT: mucous membranes moist, no scleral icterus. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm; no
murmur; well perfused. Respiratory: Clear to diminished; good air movement; tolerating trach collar. Abdomen: soft, non-distended,
+bowel sounds; PEG site clean and dry. Extremities: pulses intact. Neuro: Alert and oriented; CAM-ICU negative; strength improving
with rehab. Skin/Lines: Skin intact; healing well; ambulating with assistance.
Laboratory Data (Pertinent)
CBC: WBC 6.0 x103/uL, Hgb 9.6 g/dL, Hct 29%, platelets 232 x109/L (neutrophils 72%). BMP: Na 138, K 4.3, Cl 102, CO2 24, BUN 20,
creatinine 1.03 mg/dL, glucose 148 mg/dL, Ca 8.4, Mg 2.2, Phos 3.3. ABG (07:00): pH 7.38 / PaCO2 35 / PaO2 88 / HCO3 23; lactate
1.2 mmol/L; P/F ratio 281.
Imaging (Pertinent)
No new imaging obtained today. Most recent radiograph reviewed and compared; findings consistent with the documented clinical
trajectory.
Condition & Functional Status at Transfer
Alert, oriented, conversant. Nasal cannula at 2 L. Ambulating with walker; sternal precautions maintained. Tolerating heart-healthy diet.
Sternal wound with negative-pressure dressing, granulating. Off vasopressors and inotropes. Hemodynamically stable on oral
goal-directed medical therapy.
Transfer Medications
Medication | Dose | Route | Frequency | Indication
[p.1038] Aspirin | 81 mg | PO | Daily | Post-STEMI/CABG
Ticagrelor | 90 mg | PO | BID | Post-PCI/DAPT
Atorvastatin | 80 mg | PO | QHS | Post-STEMI
Carvedilol | 25 mg | PO | BID | HFrEF, post-STEMI
Lisinopril | 20 mg | PO | Daily | HFrEF, post-STEMI
Spironolactone | 25 mg | PO | Daily | HFrEF
Empagliflozin | 10 mg | PO | Daily | HFrEF, T2DM
Apixaban | 5 mg | PO | BID | DVT and post-op AF
Cefazolin | 2 g | IV | q8h (finish course) | Sternal wound infection
Furosemide | 20 mg | PO | Daily | HFrEF
Insulin glargine | 20 units | SC | QHS | T2DM
Insulin aspart | sliding scale | SC | with meals | T2DM
Pantoprazole | 40 mg | PO | Daily | Stress ulcer prophylaxis
Acetaminophen | 650 mg | PO | q6h PRN | Pain/fever
Follow-Up & Recommendations
1. Continue cardiac rehabilitation phase I; transition to phase II outpatient after discharge from rehab facility.
2. Cardiology follow-up in 2 weeks; repeat TTE in 3 months for LVEF reassessment.
3. CT surgery follow-up in 2 weeks for sternal wound and post-CABG status.
4. Complete cefazolin course; ID follow-up.
5. Continue anticoagulation; hematology follow-up.
6. Diabetes management; primary care and endocrinology follow-up.
7. Sternal precautions for 8 weeks post-CABG (no lifting > 5 lbs; log-roll; no arm push-off).
8. Return precautions: chest pain, shortness of breath, sternal wound problems, signs of infection, palpitations, bleeding.

History of Present Illness

gallop; JVD to angle of jaw. Respiratory: tachypneic; bilateral crackles to mid-lung fields. Abdomen: soft, non-tender. Extremities: cool

Assessment
50-year-old man with acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock requiring mechanical circulatory

EDUCATION
Documented teaching with teach-back; per-medication education included
[p.668] Clinician Note: Per-medication education is provided at initiation of each new medication and at discharge. Teach-back is documented
for each session. Learning barriers: critical illness and delirium early in the course; participation improved with recovery. Interpreter not
required (English).
Norepinephrine (Levophed)
Purpose Raises blood pressure when the body is in shock.
Dose & Route Titrated via IV infusion to maintain blood pressure.
Side Effects Decreased blood flow to hands/feet; irregular heartbeat.
Monitoring Continuous blood pressure and heart rate monitoring.
Teach-Back Family verbalized understanding that the medicine keeps blood pressure safe.
Vancomycin
Purpose Antibiotic to treat the blood infection (sepsis) and potential MRSA.
Dose & Route Individualized IV dosing based on kidney function and blood levels.
Side Effects Kidney injury (monitored daily); rash if given too fast (Red Man Syndrome).
Monitoring Daily labs; infuse slowly over at least 60 minutes.
Teach-Back Family able to state purpose; instructed to report rash or skin flushing.
Piperacillin-tazobactam (Zosyn)
Purpose Broad-spectrum antibiotic targeting pneumonia and gram-negative bacteria.
Dose & Route 4.5 g IV every 6 hours, extended infusion over 3 hours.
Side Effects Diarrhea; low potassium; allergic reaction (report rash immediately).
Monitoring Renal function, electrolytes daily.
Teach-Back Teach-back deferred - patient sedated. Education provided to son.
Pantoprazole (Protonix)
Purpose Protects the stomach lining while on stress-ulcer prophylaxis.
Dose & Route 40 mg IV once daily, transitioning to oral when tolerating feeds.
Side Effects Low magnesium with long-term use (monitored); headache.
Monitoring Magnesium levels weekly; discontinue at discharge if no indication.
Teach-Back Patient verbalized that medication protects the stomach.
Enoxaparin (Lovenox)
Purpose Blood thinner to prevent blood clots (DVT) in legs and lungs.
Dose & Route Prophylactic dose; adjusted if active clot is confirmed.
Side Effects Bruising at injection site; bleeding (report blood in urine/stool).
[p.681] Monitoring Daily CBC; watch for signs of bleeding.
Teach-Back Son acknowledged understanding of clot-prevention purpose and verbalized when to call
for help (unusual bleeding).
Insulin infusion / Sliding scale
Purpose Controls blood sugar (glucose) which rises during critical illness.
Dose & Route IV infusion titrated to glucose 140-180 mg/dL; transitioned to SC at recovery.
Side Effects
Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia): sweating, confusion, shakiness.
Monitoring Point-of-care glucose every 1-2 hours while on infusion.
Teach-Back Patient able to describe symptoms of low blood sugar at discharge planning.
Amiodarone
Purpose Corrects and prevents rapid irregular heartbeat (atrial fibrillation).
Dose & Route IV load then oral maintenance; dose adjusted per response.
Side Effects Thyroid problems, lung toxicity, liver effects (all monitored). Sensitivity to sunlight - use
sunscreen.
Monitoring Thyroid/liver labs monthly; chest X-ray annually; QT interval on ECG.
Teach-Back Family verbalized that patient needs ongoing monitoring after discharge. Written materials
provided.
Apixaban (Eliquis) - at discharge
Purpose Blood thinner for catheter-associated DVT (blood clot in neck vein).
Dose & Route 10 mg twice daily x 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily x at least 3 months.
Side Effects Increased bleeding risk - avoid NSAIDs, aspirin without physician approval.
Monitoring No routine lab monitoring required, but report unusual bleeding.
Teach-Back Patient and son demonstrated understanding of dose schedule and verbalized to avoid
ibuprofen. Written instruction sheet given.

[p.155] Patient: [[NAME-0004]]
Date: 2027-02-14
Destination: Cardiac Rehabilitation Facility
Why You Are Being Transferred: You are being transferred to a cardiac rehabilitation facility to continue building your
strength, care for your surgical wound, and complete your recovery from the heart attack and heart surgery.
Your Diagnoses (Plain Language)
You had a large heart attack that caused your heart to weaken (heart failure). We put in a special heart pump to help you, and later did
open-heart surgery to bypass the blocked arteries. You also had a wound infection at your surgery site and a blood clot in your leg, both
of which are being treated. Your heart is stronger now with the help of medications and rehabilitation.
Medicines
Take all medications exactly as listed. These are very important for your heart. This includes two blood thinners (aspirin and ticagrelor for
your stents; apixaban for the leg clot), a cholesterol medication, four medications to help your heart muscle recover (carvedilol, lisinopril,
spironolactone, empagliflozin), a water pill (furosemide), and diabetes medications. Do not stop any medications without talking to your
doctors.
Activity
Follow sternal precautions for 8 weeks after surgery: do not lift more than 5 pounds, do not push up with your arms, and log-roll when
getting out of bed. Participate fully in cardiac rehabilitation. Walk regularly and increase activity as instructed. No driving for 4-6 weeks
after surgery.
Diet & Feeding
Follow a heart-healthy, low-sodium, diabetic diet. Limit salt to less than 2000 mg per day. Weigh yourself daily at the same time; report
weight gain of more than 2 pounds in a day or 5 pounds in a week.
Devices, Lines & Wounds
Your surgical wound has a negative-pressure vacuum dressing. The rehab facility will manage the wound care and eventually transition
to a regular dressing. Report increased redness, drainage, pain, or fever.
Equipment / Supplies Arranged
Walker for ambulation, wound care supplies for sternal wound, glucose monitor, digital scale, and blood pressure cuff - coordinated with
the cardiac rehabilitation facility and durable medical equipment vendor.
Follow-Up Appointments
Specialty | When | Purpose
Cardiology | 2 weeks | Post-STEMI/CABG follow-up, medication titration
Cardiothoracic Surgery | 2 weeks | Sternal wound and post-CABG assessment
Infectious Diseases | Per rehab facility | Complete antibiotic course
Cardiac Rehabilitation (Phase II) | After rehab discharge | Outpatient exercise program
Primary Care | After rehab discharge | Overall care, diabetes management
Hematology / Anticoagulation | 1-2 weeks | DVT anticoagulation management
When to Get Help Immediately
[p.1034] Call for help right away for: chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, fainting, weight gain more than 2 lbs overnight or 5 lbs in a week,
sternal wound problems (redness, drainage, opening, or fever), leg swelling or pain, bleeding, or signs of stroke.
Electronically signed: Douglas Fairfax, MD, Cardiovascular Critical Care (Attending)   |   2027-02-14"}]}

Admission Diagnoses
Acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock
Discharge / Transfer Diagnoses
Resolved acute anterior STEMI status post primary PCI to LAD and emergency 3-vessel CABG; heart failure with reduced ejection
fraction (EF 35-40%); resolved cardiogenic shock; resolved post-cardiac-arrest state with intact neurologic function; resolved
post-cardiotomy atrial fibrillation; contrast-induced AKI with renal recovery; superficial sternal wound infection (MSSA) on cefazolin with
wound VAC; right popliteal DVT on apixaban; type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension; hyperlipidemia; ICU-acquired weakness.
Hospital Course
[[NAME-0004]] presented with acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock. Emergency primary
PCI to the proximal LAD achieved TIMI 2 flow with residual multivessel disease. Impella CP and intra-aortic balloon pump were placed for
hemodynamic support, and the patient was intubated for pulmonary edema. The course was complicated by contrast-induced acute
kidney injury (KDIGO 2, non-dialysis), pulseless ventricular tachycardia arrest on ICU day 4 with successful ROSC after 8 minutes of
ACLS and targeted temperature management, and cardiogenic shock refractory to medical therapy. After multidisciplinary heart-team
evaluation, emergency 3-vessel coronary artery bypass grafting (LIMA to LAD, SVG to OM1 and RCA) was performed on ICU day 7 with
difficult wean from cardiopulmonary bypass. The post-operative course was complicated by post-cardiotomy hypotension requiring
transfusion, failed extubation from flash pulmonary edema with reintubation on ICU day 11, new-onset atrial fibrillation post-cardiotomy
controlled with amiodarone, a superficial sternal wound infection with methicillin-susceptible S. aureus treated with cefazolin and wound
VAC therapy, catheter-associated right popliteal DVT treated with therapeutic anticoagulation, and profound ICU-acquired weakness.
Repeat coronary angiography demonstrated patent grafts. Ejection fraction improved from 15-20% to 35-40% on goal-directed medical
therapy. The patient is transferred to a cardiac rehabilitation facility for continued reconditioning, sternal wound follow-up, and cardiac
rehabilitation.

billed claim line. You are given, below, everything a retrieval step already queried from a

Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

Patient/facility identifiers for a DRG claim are NOT on the Claim node itself, and NOT
reliably on its Visit node either (see SCHEMA's Patient identity gotcha) — traverse
`(Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)` to get them, or, for MR_01..MR_10 only,
look them up on the paired readmission claim.

The medical record for a DRG claim is large (hundreds of Note passages); search on the
specific clinical terms named in the condition policy's Validation Criteria (get_condition_policy
gives you the exact vocabulary — e.g. "endotracheal", "purulent", "PaO2/FiO2") rather than a
generic term.

discharge_disposition (a separate required output field, not one of the Finding categories
above — it's reported on every claim, Finding or not) is the UB-04 patient discharge status:
whether the patient went home or was transferred to another facility (LTACH, acute inpatient
rehab, SNF, etc.), which matters for post-acute-care-transfer payment policy. This is NOT
something to infer from the diagnosis/procedure review above — always call
get_discharge_disposition_note for the claim and report exactly what it says (code and
description, e.g. "63 - Discharged/transferred to LTACH"); null only if it returns no rows.


Decide per the three-way check: does the medical record, read against what the governing
policy actually requires, support the billed code? Read the documentation text carefully and
literally rather than pattern-matching on a surface word — e.g. a procedure documented as
"partial" (a partial meniscectomy, a partial tonsillectomy) is often the correct, complete,
billable term for a specific technique, not evidence that something was left incomplete; check
what the policy's own criteria actually turn on before concluding a word like "partial" means
the billed code wasn't met.

Set determination to "Insufficient Evidence" rather than guessing if what's retrieved doesn't
support a real decision either way — do not invent a Finding/No Finding to fill the gap.

system_note is the auditor note a human reviewer reads on EVERY claim, Finding or not — write
it with explicit citations (document/section/page) and reasoning a reviewer could audit line by
line; a correct determination with a
vague, citation-free note still scores as a weak note (see the quality bar in the schema
field's own description).

rationale_letter is a SEPARATE, formal appeal-ready letter to the provider — only written when
determination is Finding (null otherwise). It restates the finding and its basis for an
external, non-technical reader, not a repeat of system_note's internal auditor reasoning.

Page numbers: a medical-record note can span several PDF pages, and its page_start/page_end
are not the page of any particular line in it. In a long note's text, a [p.N] marker means the
text after it (up to the next marker) is on physical page N; cite that page in system_note,
never a note's page_start/page_end range. A note whose page_start equals its page_end is all on
that page. In a multi-page note with no marker before the line, name the note without a page.

evidence_cited must reference only passages that actually appear in the retrieved rows above.
Each entry is the source_id of the one row the quote comes from, copied exactly, and the quote
copied verbatim from that row's text, character for character: don't wrap part of it in
quotation marks, fix a typo, or drop a word or code from the middle. Never invent or recall one. Code checks each quote
against that row and fills in the document, section and page from it, so a quote that isn't in
the cited row, or a source_id that wasn't retrieved, is dropped. Each quote is ONE contiguous
passage from a single row: if you need two separate passages, give two separate evidence_cited
entries rather than joining them with "..."; a stitched-together quote can't be verified. Rows
with no source_id (claim lines, code descriptions, a tool's own summary rows) aren't citable;
cite the record or policy row behind them instead.

Education provided to son.\nPantoprazole (Protonix)\nPurpose Protects the stomach lining while on stress-ulcer prophylaxis.\nDose & Route 40 mg IV once daily, transitioning to oral when tolerating feeds.\nSide Effects Low magnesium with long-term use (monitored); headache.\nMonitoring Magnesium levels weekly; discontinue at discharge if no indication.\nTeach-Back Patient verbalized that medication protects the stomach.\nEnoxaparin (Lovenox)\nPurpose Blood thinner to prevent blood clots (DVT) in legs and lungs.\nDose & Route Prophylactic dose; adjusted if active clot is confirmed.\nSide Effects Bruising at injection site; bleeding (report blood in urine/stool).\n[p.681] Monitoring Daily CBC; watch for signs of bleeding.\nTeach-Back Son acknowledged understanding of clot-prevention purpose and verbalized when to call\nfor help (unusual bleeding).\nInsulin infusion / Sliding scale\nPurpose Controls blood sugar (glucose) which rises during critical illness.\nDose & Route IV infusion titrated to glucose 140-180 mg/dL; transitioned to SC at recovery.\nSide Effects\nLow blood sugar (hypoglycemia): sweating, confusion, shakiness.\nMonitoring Point-of-care glucose every 1-2 hours while on infusion.\nTeach-Back Patient able to describe symptoms of low blood sugar at discharge planning.\nAmiodarone\nPurpose Corrects and prevents rapid irregular heartbeat (atrial fibrillation).\nDose & Route IV load then oral maintenance; dose adjusted per response.\nSide Effects Thyroid problems, lung toxicity, liver effects (all monitored). Sensitivity to sunlight - use\nsunscreen.\nMonitoring Thyroid/liver labs monthly; chest X-ray annually; QT interval on ECG.\nTeach-Back Family verbalized that patient needs ongoing monitoring after discharge. Written materials\nprovided.\nApixaban (Eliquis) - at discharge\nPurpose Blood thinner for catheter-associated DVT (blood clot in neck vein).\nDose & Route 10 mg twice daily x 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily x at least 3 months.\nSide Effects Increased bleeding risk - avoid NSAIDs, aspirin without physician approval.\nMonitoring No routine lab monitoring required, but report unusual bleeding.\nTeach-Back Patient and son demonstrated understanding of dose schedule and verbalized to avoid\nibuprofen. We put in a special heart pump to help you, and later did\nopen-heart surgery to bypass the blocked arteries. You also had a wound infection at your surgery site and a blood clot in your leg, both\nof which are being treated. Your heart is stronger now with the help of medications and rehabilitation.\nMedicines\nTake all medications exactly as listed. These are very important for your heart. This includes two blood thinners (aspirin and ticagrelor for\nyour stents; apixaban for the leg clot), a cholesterol medication, four medications to help your heart muscle recover (carvedilol, lisinopril,\nspironolactone, empagliflozin), a water pill (furosemide), and diabetes medications. Do not stop any medications without talking to your\ndoctors.\nActivity\nFollow sternal precautions for 8 weeks after surgery: do not lift more than 5 pounds, do not push up with your arms, and log-roll when\ngetting out of bed. Participate fully in cardiac rehabilitation. Walk regularly and increase activity as instructed. No driving for 4-6 weeks\nafter surgery.\nDiet & Feeding\nFollow a heart-healthy, low-sodium, diabetic diet. Limit salt to less than 2000 mg per day. Weigh yourself daily at the same time; report\nweight gain of more than 2 pounds in a day or 5 pounds in a week.\nDevices, Lines & Wounds\nYour surgical wound has a negative-pressure vacuum dressing. The rehab facility will manage the wound care and eventually transition\nto a regular dressing. Report increased redness, drainage, pain, or fever.\nEquipment / Supplies Arranged\nWalker for ambulation, wound care supplies for sternal wound, glucose monitor, digital scale, and blood pressure cuff - coordinated with\nthe cardiac rehabilitation facility and durable medical equipment vendor.\nFollow-Up Appointments\nSpecialty | When | Purpose\nCardiology | 2 weeks | Post-STEMI/CABG follow-up, medication titration\nCardiothoracic Surgery | 2 weeks | Sternal wound and post-CABG assessment\nInfectious Diseases | Per rehab facility | Complete antibiotic course\nCardiac Rehabilitation (Phase II) | After rehab discharge | Outpatient exercise program\nPrimary Care | After rehab discharge | Overall care, diabetes management\nHematology / Anticoagulation | 1-2 weeks | DVT anticoagulation management\nWhen to Get Help Immediately\n[p.1034] Call for help right away for: chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, fainting, weight gain more than 2 lbs overnight or 5 lbs in a week,\nsternal wound problems (redness, drainage, opening, or fever), leg swelling or pain, bleeding, or signs of stroke.\nElectronically signed: Douglas Fairfax, MD, Cardiovascular Critical Care (Attending)   |   2027-02-14"}]}

result.system_note: MR_26 (admit 2026-10-08 -> discharge/transfer 2027-02-14). Review of the medical record against the governing DRG policies shows multiple coding/POA discrepancies requiring correction. Summary of what was billed and what the record shows (key citations): - Principal diagnosis billed: I21.09 (STEMI). Supported: History & Physical (Admitting), p.142 documents an acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock on presentation (ev1: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_26.pdf-n9, History & Physical (Admitting), p.142). Interventional Cardiology documents primary PCI to proximal LAD and residual multivessel disease (ev2: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_26.pdf-n12, Interventional Cardiology Consultation, p.34). Discharge/Transfer Summary lists reason for admission as acute anterior STEMI with cardiogenic shock (ev3: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_26.pdf-n1108, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037). Principal sequencing to an acute anterior STEMI is supported by documentation (principal stays I21.x). - Cardiogenic shock (R57.0, billed POA=Y, MCC): supported. Interventional note and H&P document cardiogenic shock with placement of mechanical circulatory support (Impella CP and IABP) (ev2: Interventional Cardiology Consultation, p.34). Policy requires provider documentation and either hemodynamic instability evidence or MCS placement to validate R57.0 (ev13: RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Cardiogenic-Shock.docx-b27). The record meets those criteria (ev1, ev2). - Cardiac arrest (I46.9, billed POA=Y, MCC): not present on admission per the timeline. Discharge summary documents a pulseless ventricular tachycardia arrest on ICU day 4 with ROSC after 8 minutes and TTM (ev3: Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037). Policy for I46.9 requires documentation of a pulseless arrest event and ROSC; sequencing depends on whether arrest was present on arrival or occurred during the encounter (ev15: RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Cardiac-Arrest-with-Return-of-Spontaneous-Circulation.docx-b27). Because the arrest occurred on ICU day 4, the POA flag should be N (not present on admission), not Y as billed. - Acute kidney injury (N17.9, billed POA=N, CC): mixed timeline in the chart but provider documentation on the admitting note and nephrology consult confirm AKI related to contrast/shock. The H&P lists AKI and shows creatinine elevated on presentation (creatinine 1.4, baseline 0.9) and includes AKI on the active problem list (ev1: History & Physical (Admitting), p.142). Nephrology documents KDIGO stage 2 contrast-induced AKI with creatinine peak 2.8 and oliguria (ev4: Nephrology Consultation, p.116). Policy requires provider documentation of AKI and KDIGO objective evidence to validate N17.9 (ev16: RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Kidney-Injury.docx-b29). Because the admitting documentation already includes AKI and objective abnormal creatinine, the record supports AKI being present on admission (POA=Y) or at minimum documents it contemporaneously with initial presentation; the billed POA=N is not consistent with the admitting H&P evidence. (Change POA to Y is supported by ev1 and ev4.) - Acute respiratory failure with hypoxia (J96.01, billed POA=Y, MCC): supported. H&P and interventional progress notes document severe hypoxemia (ABG PaO2 62 on NRB; SpO2 88%) and need for invasive airway/mechanical ventilation; discharge and progress notes document intubation for pulmonary edema and subsequent trach-collar tolerance (ev9: History & Physical (Admitting), p.142; ev7 & ev8: Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037). Policy for J96.01 allows presumption of objective hypoxemia when invasive mechanical ventilation is initiated and attributed to respiratory failure (ev14: RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Failure-with-Hypoxia.docx-b27 and RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Failure-with-Hypoxia.docx-b37). J96.01 as billed appears supported and POA=Y is reasonable. - New-onset post-operative atrial fibrillation (I48.91, billed POA=N, CC): supported as hospital-acquired. Discharge summary documents 'new-onset atrial fibrillation post-cardiotomy controlled with amiodarone' (ev10: Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037). Policy requires provider documentation of new-onset post-op AF and documentation of management (ev15: RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Atrial-Fibrillation.docx-b27). POA=N is appropriate. - Procedure-related infection and MSSA (T81.4XXA, T81.89XA, B95.61 billed POA=N): supported. Discharge diagnoses and hospital course identify a superficial sternal wound infection with MSSA treated with cefazolin and wound VAC (ev5: Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037). These are hospital-acquired (POA=N) and supported by documentation. - Deep venous thrombosis (I82.402 billed = left lower extremity): discharge and transfer notes specify a right popliteal DVT on apixaban (ev5: Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037). The billed left-sided DVT (I82.402) is not supported; the correct reported location is right popliteal DVT. The billed code should be revised to the right-sided DVT code (recode I82.402 -> I82.401, see code_decisions). Policy-level side/late specification issues aside, the documentation clearly identifies the DVT on the right, not left. - Do-Not-Resuscitate (Z66, billed POA=Y): unsupported. The Patient Facesheet on admission documents 'Code Status Full Code' (ev6: Patient Facesheet, p.4). No contemporaneous documentation supports a DNR in the chart; palliative consulted but family elected to proceed with aggressive interventions (ev11: Palliative Care Consultation, p.334). Remove Z66 from the coded list. Procedures (summary): - PCI to proximal LAD, Impella CP placement, and IABP placement are documented (ev2: Interventional Cardiology Consultation, p.34; ev7: Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037). CABG 3-vessel with LIMA to LAD and SVG to OM1 and RCA is documented (ev3: Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037). Intubation and prolonged ventilation including trach collar tolerance are documented (ev7, ev8), which supports mechanical ventilation >96 hours (5A1D90Z). Continuous cardiac output monitoring / mixed venous monitoring documented on admission orders supports 5A1221Z (ev11: History & Physical (Admitting), p.142). Unresolved conflict requiring human review: - Operative/procedure-side discrepancy for saphenous vein harvest (billing lists excision of right saphenous vein, 06BQ0ZZ, while another operative line in the chart indicates left saphenous harvest). The record contains conflicting lines flagged as CONFLICT-00194; the dataset does not include a resolved operative note we can rely on. I recommend human verification of the operative record to confirm the harvest side and correct ICD-10-PCS laterality (see hitl_question: CONFLICT-00194). Because the operative laterality cannot be resolved from the retrieved rows, this single-item ambiguity is escalated to HITL despite the overall DRG-level finding. Net action taken in this audit (claim-level): - Finding: Billing requires correction for POA flags (I46.9 should be POA=N; N17.9 POA should be Y per admitting H&P and nephrology documentation), removal of unsupported diagnosis Z66 (Do not resuscitate), and recoding of left lower-extremity DVT (I82.402) to right-sided DVT (I82.401) per discharge documentation. All other billed diagnoses and procedures are supported by the record and applicable DRG policy criteria (citations above). Per the Cardiac Arrest policy, I46.x is sequenced/POA per the documented timing; because arrest occurred during the hospitalization, POA should be N, not Y (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Cardiac-Arrest-with-Return-of-Spontaneous-Circulation.docx-b27; ev15). We will change POA to N. 2) N17.9 (Acute kidney failure) - POA indicator should be reviewed/changed to Y. Nephrology documents KDIGO stage 2 contrast-induced AKI with creatinine peak 2.8 (Nephrology Consultation, p.116; ev4). Policy requires provider documentation plus KDIGO objective criteria to validate N17.9 (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Kidney-Injury.docx-b29; ev16). Given the admitting documentation and objective labs, N17.9 should be POA=Y (present on admission) rather than POA=N. 3) I82.402 (Acute embolism and thrombosis of unspecified deep veins of left lower extremity) - side/location mismatch. The Discharge / Transfer Summary documents a right popliteal DVT on apixaban (ev5). The billed left-sided DVT is not supported; the code should be changed to the appropriate right-sided DVT code (recode to I82.401 per the chart) to reflect the documented right popliteal DVT. 4) Z66 (Do not resuscitate) - unsupported by the contemporaneous record. The Patient Facesheet (admit) documents Code Status: Full Code (Patient Facesheet, p.4; ev6) and the palliative consult documents goals-of-care discussion with family electing to proceed (Palliative Care Consultation, p.334; ev11). code_decisions.reason: Cardiac arrest is documented as occurring on ICU day 4 with ROSC and TTM (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037; ev3). Policy requires POA reflect timing; arrest was not present on admission so POA should be N.

Admitting H&P documents AKI with elevated creatinine on presentation and nephrology documents KDIGO stage 2 contrast-induced AKI (History & Physical (Admitting), p.142; Nephrology Consultation, p.116; ev1, ev4). Policy requires provider documentation/KDIGO evidence to validate N17.9 (ev16); POA should be Y per admitting documentation.

Discharge summary documents new-onset post-cardiotomy atrial fibrillation controlled with amiodarone (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037; ev10). Policy supports post-op AF as not present on admission.
Post-procedural complications (post-cardiotomy hypotension, failed extubation, wound infection) are documented in the hospital course (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037; ev3).
Superficial sternal wound infection after CABG with MSSA is documented (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037; ev5).
MSSA identified as pathogen for the sternal wound infection in discharge diagnoses (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037; ev5).

Discharge documentation specifies a right popliteal DVT (right lower extremity) (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037; ev5). Billed code for left-sided DVT (I82.402) is not supported. Recode to the matching right-sided DVT code (I82.401).

Interventional and admission notes document multivessel atherosclerotic coronary disease and prior CAD history consistent with I25.10 (Interventional Cardiology Consultation, p.34; History & Physical (Admitting), p.434; ev2, ev12).
Type 2 diabetes mellitus is listed on the discharge diagnoses and in the admitting history (ev5, ev12).
Hypertension is documented in past medical history on the admitting H&P (History & Physical (Admitting), p.434; ev12).
Hyperlipidemia is documented in the admitting history (History & Physical (Admitting), p.434; ev12).

Patient was documented as 'Full Code' on the Patient Facesheet at admission and palliative consult documents family elected to proceed with aggressive care; no DNR documentation found (Patient Facesheet, p.4; Palliative Care Consultation, p.334; ev6, ev11). Remove Z66.
Percutaneous drug-eluting stent placement (primary PCI) to LAD is documented (Interventional Cardiology Consultation, p.34; ev2).
Impella CP placement (short-term percutaneous heart assist) is documented (Interventional Cardiology Consultation, p.34; Discharge summary, p.1037; ev2, ev7).
Intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) placement is documented (Interventional Cardiology Consultation, p.34; Discharge summary, p.1037; ev2, ev7).
CABG with grafting is documented in the discharge summary (emergency 3-vessel CABG; ev3). Specific PCS mapping to number of graft sites will be verified; documentation supports CABG performed.
CABG with multiple graft sites is documented; the operative report documents LIMA to LAD and SVG grafts (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037; ev3).

Saphenous-vein grafts are documented (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037; ev3). However, there is a documented conflict in the operative notes regarding the side of harvest (CONFLICT-00194). Human review required to confirm laterality and correctness of 06BQ0ZZ; procedure retained pending HITL confirmation.
Endotracheal intubation is documented early in the course for pulmonary edema (History & Physical, p.142; Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037; ev9, ev7).
Prolonged mechanical ventilation is documented including reintubation and later trach-collar tolerance, supporting ventilation >96 consecutive hours (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037; ev7, ev8).

Continuous cardiac output / mixed venous monitoring is ordered and documented in admission orders and hemodynamic monitoring plan (History & Physical (Admitting), p.142; Interventional Cardiology Consultation, p.34; ev1, ev11).
